description: THE FILTER IS UNGATED AND THE SECOND PAINT WINS - the one case in this directory whose subject is the POSITION of app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:136-143 rather than the value it reads. Read the directory's authorisation-filter cases as a set: case06, case08 and case09 drive the filter with a subscript below, inside-but-unvalued and far beyond the declared table and prove the read is bounded; case11 and case12 reach the filter clean, with no prior rejection, and prove its true arm; this case is the only one where BOTH the validation IF and the filter IF fire in a single pass, which is what proves the filter is not gated by the error flag and not an ELSE of the validation above it. The path, statement by statement. The commarea carries CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1, so 88 CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:31 holds and the IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :87 is false - this is the REENTER side of gate G38, the ENTER side being case02 and case20, and it matters that it is REENTER because :89's MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COMEN1AO belongs to the other branch and does not run here. :92 receives the map and :93-95 take the DFHENTER arm of EVALUATE EIBAID into PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. The descending test-before scan at :117-121 examines OPTIONI OF COMEN1AI(2:1), finds the '3' already non-blank and exits at once with WS-IDX = 2, so the two-byte move at :122 into WS-OPTION-X PIC X(02) JUST RIGHT at :45 needs no right-justification and the INSPECT REPLACING ALL ' ' BY '0' at :123 is a no-op - unlike case06, whose leading blank is exactly what that INSPECT turns into a zero. :124 leaves WS-OPTION PIC 9(02) at :46 holding 3 and :125 echoes it, which is why OPTIONO is '03' and not spaces. The three-term guard at :127-129 is then evaluated in source order, gate G30. Term one, WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC, is false because '03' is numeric. Term two, WS-OPTION > CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT, is TRUE against this case's option table, whose active count is 1. Term three, WS-OPTION = ZEROS, is never reached. :130 moves 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, which is the 88 ERR-FLG-ON condition at :41; :131-132 move the thirty-seven-character 'Please enter a valid option number...' into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at :38; :133 performs SEND-MENU-SCREEN, and that is the first paint. Why the table is a stub and what the stub varies. app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy:21 declares CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT PIC 9(02) VALUE 10 and every one of the ten valued CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE columns is 'U' (:29, :35, :41, :47, :53, :59, :65, :72, :78, :84), so the filter's true arm is unreachable from the shipped table and no case seeded from real data could ever make both IF statements fire. The table used here therefore values slots 1, 2, 3 and 4 with the copybook's own CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME and CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME literals, changes slot 3's authorisation column alone to 'A', and declares an active count of 1. Two consequences follow from that single count, and both are the point: option 3 exceeds it, so the validation rejects; and slot 3 is nevertheless a valued entry, so the filter above the count still finds a real 'A' to compare. Nothing else about the shipped table is altered, so the authorisation column is the only variable under test. The substance. PERFORM SEND-MENU-SCREEN is a PERFORM and a PERFORM RETURNS, so control reaches :136 with WS-ERR-FLG already 'Y'. :136-137 are not an ELSE of :127-134 and carry no IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON guard of their own. The first conjunct, 88 CDEMO-USRTYP-USER at app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:28 VALUE 'U', is true because the commarea supplies CDEMO-USER-TYPE 'U' - load-bearing, because 'A' would short-circuit the conjunction and the subscript would never be read at all. The second conjunct reads CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE(3) and finds 'A'. :138 SET ERR-FLG-ON TO TRUE - a SET here where :130 used MOVE 'Y', two spellings of one state that a translation must not let drift apart; :139 moves SPACES over WS-MESSAGE; :140-141 move the thirty-three-character 'No access - Admin Only option... ' literal, whose trailing space padding to PIC X(80) makes invisible; :142 performs SEND-MENU-SCREEN again. The second paint overwrites the first, so the terminal shows the refusal and the expectation on the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel is that thirty-three-character literal plus forty-seven spaces, eighty characters exactly - NOT the thirty-seven-character option rejection that :131-132 put there first. Hoist the filter into the validation's ELSE, or move it below the dispatch at :145, and this case carries the option rejection instead: the position of the filter between the two other IF statements is behaviour, and this is the fixture that says so. What the single send does and does not claim. The unit kind is SERVICE, so MainMenuService is constructed and called as a plain object with no MockMvc, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path, which is gate G51. What the fingerprint carries is the final MainMenuOutcome - the state the second paint left - so the send count is one and the two-paint sequence is proven by the identity of the surviving message rather than by a count of two. Stated plainly so nobody reads more into the count than it holds: this fixture proves which image survives, and the SERVICE projection is not the place where a lost send would show up. The suppressed dispatch, and every absence it explains. :145's IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is false, so the whole of :146-164 is skipped and each of its side effects is missing from the expectation for that one reason: no EXEC CICS XCTL at :152-155, so no successor is named and the termination is the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) of :107-110 rather than a transfer; CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT stays 1 because the MOVE ZEROS at :151 never runs, which is also what makes this response a legal next request; CDEMO-FROM-TRANID and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM keep their inbound 'CC00' and 'COSGN00C' because :147-148 never run; and ERRMSGC is never overridden, because the MOVE DFHGREEN at :158 sits inside that same block. The colour, which is easy to misread. ERRMSGC is pinned as DFHRED, and that is the map's DECLARED colour and not something the program moved: app/bms/COMEN01.bms:154-157 is ERRMSG DFHMDF ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET), COLOR=RED, LENGTH=78. COMEN01C contains no MOVE DFHRED anywhere in its 282 lines and copies no CSSETATY, so the DFHRED-plus-asterisk field highlight that COACTUPC applies has no counterpart here and none is expected; the only colour this program ever moves is DFHGREEN at :158, on the coming-soon path alone, which is how the screen tells a refusal from a confirmation. A refusal therefore stays red by default, and pinning the attribute rather than omitting it is what keeps that default asserted instead of merely unchecked. The menu lines, and the dead arms that stay dead. BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS at :236-277 loops PERFORM VARYING WS-IDX FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL WS-IDX > CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT, which is the stub's 1, so only the WHEN 1 arm at :249-250 fires. OPTN001O is composed by the STRING at :243-246 as CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM(1) then '. ' then CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME(1) into WS-MENU-OPT-TXT PIC X(40) at :48, giving '01. ' plus the thirty-five-byte 'Account View' name and one pad byte - forty characters, byte-identical to the line the shipped table would compose. The other eleven lines are the unpainted image, forty U+0000 bytes each and NOT spaces, because the map area was last set to LOW-VALUES and this pass writes only one line. The WHEN 11, WHEN 12 and WHEN OTHER arms at :269-274 are unreachable here for the same reason they are unreachable with the shipped count of ten, and they are preserved dead code: extending the loop to twelve iterations to 'use' the declared slots would be a behaviour change, not a fix. Geometry a reviewer can confirm by eye. Each table entry is CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM PIC 9(02) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME PIC X(35) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME PIC X(08) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE PIC X(01) at app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy:89-92, so 2 + 35 + 8 + 1 = 46 bytes. The data division gives VALUE clauses to ten entries at :25-84, 10 x 46 = 460 bytes, while CDEMO-MENU-OPTIONS REDEFINES CDEMO-MENU-OPTIONS-DATA at :87 spans CDEMO-MENU-OPT OCCURS 12 TIMES at :88, 12 x 46 = 552 bytes - so 92 bytes, exactly slots 11 and 12, have no backing literal at all. That oversized REDEFINES is a legacy defect and is preserved rather than repaired, as is the ungated filter itself: the subscript read is bounded to the declared OCCURS 1..12 so that no Java exception appears where COBOL without SSRANGE would have read stray bytes, and nothing else about either construct is corrected. Because COBOL subscripts are 1-based and Java indices are 0-based, subscript 3 must address the THIRD entry, and it is the third entry alone that carries 'A' here - so a translation reading index 3 of a 0-based table would find slot 4's 'U', the filter would not fire, and this case would report the option rejection instead of the refusal. Widths for the payload come from the xxxI and xxxO items only: OPTN001O to OPTN012O are PIC X(40) at app/cpy-bms/COMEN01.CPY:182-248 and OPTIONO is PIC X(2) at :254, while OPTIONL COMP PIC S9(4), OPTIONF, OPTIONA at :127-130 and OPTIONC, OPTIONP, OPTIONH, OPTIONV at :250-253 are length, flag and attribute metadata and are never payload members. The message is pinned at the eighty bytes of WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at :38 and deliberately not at the seventy-eight of ERRMSGO PIC X(78) at COMEN01.CPY:260: the truncating MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :187 is case16's subject, and manufacturing a seventy-eight-byte field here would assert this fixture's own arithmetic instead of the program's. Statelessness, security and determinism. Every scrap of conversation state arrives in the request - EIBCALEN 160, the DFHENTER AID byte reproduced by common.CicsAid because DFHAID is IBM-supplied and absent from this repository, the sixteen-field CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and the received OPTIONI - and leaves in the response's navigation image; nothing is held server-side, which is gate G37. CDEMO-USER-TYPE is trusted exactly as the source trusts it: :149-150 are commented out, so no USRSEC read re-verifies the type and no hashing is introduced, and the legacy posture is left visible rather than quietly improved. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:33, the same instant every case in this directory pins, and the code page is named US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default. Honestly about that clock: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :212-231 does run, because SEND-MENU-SCREEN performs it at :184, and it composes CURDATEO as WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY and CURTIMEO as WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS from app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy:30-41 - but the SERVICE projection carries only the twelve menu lines and the echoed option, so neither field is surfaced here. The pinned instant buys determinism, not an assertion; the header fields belong to the CONTROLLER_POJO cases case01, case16 and case20. Provenance, and what this case does not prove. Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl, app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, app/cpy-bms/COMEN01.CPY, app/bms/COMEN01.bms and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:399-400, which defines TRANSACTION(CM00) PROGRAM(COMEN01C). None of it was captured from a live COBOL execution: no z/OS or CICS runtime exists in this environment, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, refuses a PROCEDURE DIVISION USING under -x, fails to parse app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy, and offers no Language Environment CEE services - eight verified blockers in all, recorded as risk R-A. A statically derived expectation can encode a misreading where a captured one cannot, so the limits are stated rather than glossed. This case does not prove the subscript read is bounded - case08 at 11 and case09 at 99 do that, and the twelve-slot shape with its last two slots unvalued is asserted against the model directly. It does not prove the filter's true arm reachable from a clean entry, which is case11's and case12's; it does not prove the seventy-eight-byte ERRMSGO projection, which is case16's; and it does not prove the coming-soon composition, which lives on the paths this error flag suppresses. One divergence is recorded rather than silently resolved: an alternative design for this slot would have driven OPTION 12 as the upper anchor of the OCCURS conversion, but this directory's slot is committed to ungatedness, the two subjects cannot share one fixture, and the upper anchor is held instead by the twelve-slot model assertions together with case08 and case09. What this case decisively proves is that both IF statements fire in one pass and that the second paint is the image that survives. Gates pinned: G15, G18, G30, G37, G38 on its REENTER side, and G51. HOW THE OPTION TABLE IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA: app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy carries 'U' in all ten of its CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE columns, so the true arm of the authorisation filter at app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:136-137 cannot be reached from the shipped table at all, and the OCCURS 12 slots past the populated range are storage rather than data that no dataset seeds. The table is therefore the one input to this program that cannot be expressed as a seeded row, which is why unitStimulus.environment.MENU_TABLE_VARIANT declares it. Each variant differs from the shipped table in exactly ONE column, so the authorisation column is the only variable under test and every composed menu line stays byte-identical to the real one. It is declared here rather than chosen by an adapter that recognised this file's case identifier, because an adapter keyed on an ordinal means this file gives no indication which table it runs over and renumbering it would silently move the arm to a different case. An unrecognised variant is refused by the adapter rather than ignored. This case declares ADMIN_ONLY_SLOT_THREE: four valued entries with an active count of one, the third carrying 'A' and slots 1, 2 and 4 carrying the copybook's own columns. Option 3 therefore exceeds the active count and the guard at :128 rejects it, PERFORM returns, and the UNGATED filter at :136 then finds a real 'A' at that very subscript - so both IF statements fire in one pass and line 142's paint overwrites line 133's. Which arm of the filter the adapter asserts is decided by the entered option standing ABOVE the table's active count, not by this file's name.
